LESSON: READING 3.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: how poems are broken into stanzas and stanzas into lines, 1. Why do people write poems? 2. What makes a poem interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy is achieved as the learner uses digital devices to search sources online for different poems and notes the titles and

the poets, while observing cyber safety.

Values:
Integrity is achieved as the learner searches online or offline for poems while observing cyber security.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

 Health Education is promoted as the learner tackles poems on issues such as personal hygiene, HIV and AIDS, and COVID- 19

 Cyber Safety is promoted as the learner sources online or offline for poems.

Link to other subjects

The learner relates the structure of poems to other learning areas such as Kiswahili and Creative Arts.
